A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeAR. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and visual results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and relighting evaluations in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2–4, and qualitative results and failure cases throughout the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds texture style transfer and real-world relighting demonstrations in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds a style-transfer adaptation using independently supplied target geometry for voxel coordinates and a separate style image for LH-SLAT generation. V1's inference pipeline reconstructs geometry from the input image. The underlying flow models, decoders, tokenizer and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 extends coverage to texture style transfer across different image/geometry pairs and relighting internet images and mobile photographs (Section 4.3, Figures 11–12). This adds a distinct task and real-world input conditions beyond the retained rendered-object evaluations. Training data and existing benchmark coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within Table 1's four tasks and the corresponding qualitative comparisons, including the appendix. The new applications introduce no evaluated competing methods; the new paradigm diagram uses existing baselines.

E3.justification: The added applications introduce qualitative testing with three independently paired geometry/style examples and three real-world inputs under multiple lighting/view conditions. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, rendering settings and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 illustrates the established evaluation setup.

E4.justification: Figure 12 adds qualitative generalization cases examining removal of baked-in lighting and handling of specular highlights in real-world inputs. Tables 2–4 retain the same decoder-depth, latent-input and architecture ablations, and the existing detail-loss and transparency failure cases are preserved.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. V3 does not introduce uncertainty estimation or change statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical values in Tables 1–4 and the existing appendix result panels are unchanged. Figures 11–12 add qualitative style-transfer and real-world findings. The new Figure 2 summary contains a discrepancy: its claimed Glossy Synthetic forward-rendering gain is 4.4 dB, whereas Table 1 gives 30.47 versus 25.46 dB, a 5.01 dB difference.

T1.justification: The SLAT definitions, rendering formulation, flow-matching objective and reconstruction/regularization equations are retained, including appendix Equations 7–10. No new theorem, proof, derivation or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The first contribution narrows its description from an 'end-to-end learnable' stack in v1 to a 'learnable' stack in v3; the revised pipeline caption explicitly describes end-to-end inference. The principal LH-SLAT, coupled-renderer, real-time rendering and four-task performance claims remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.2 argues for separate data-scaling needs of the two stages and scalability through model capacity and voxel resolution, without new scaling experiments. Section 4.3 interprets the added real-world examples as evidence of robustness. The existing fine-detail and transparent-material limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Hardware, LoRA configuration, optimizer schedules, training duration, loss weights, mesh-based inference and tone mapping are unchanged in the matched implementation appendices. The geometry prior highlighted in v3's pipeline figure was already disclosed in v1. Resource links provide the same access information.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Temo, TAR3D and AR-1-to-3 in Section 2.2 and expands the explicit comparison of relighting paradigms in Appendix A.1. The central positioning relative to PBR decomposition and neural rendering remains; many other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and selected related-work, decoder and limitations passages, separates LH-SLAT reconstruction and generation into subsections, and reorganizes the appendix around additional setup and discussion headings. Most method, benchmark and conclusion prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds a paradigm overview, expands the original teaser with PSNR charts, and redraws/splits the pipeline into Figures 4–5. New application panels and an evaluation schematic appear in Figures 11–12 and 14, alongside substantial figure relocation and resizing. Existing tables and appendix comparison panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearer pipeline and task diagrams, together with new style-transfer and real-world examples, modestly improve explanation and demonstrated applicability. The gains are limited because the quantitative evidence is unchanged and the new applications are qualitative. Figure 2 also introduces a reporting inconsistency: its 4.4 dB Glossy Synthetic gain conflicts with Table 1's 5.01 dB.
